questions.stem: Let $$C(x)$$ be the cost, in dollars, of producing x items. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$C'(7) = 8$$?

options.text: The average rate of change of the cost over the first 7 items is 8 dollars per item.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The cost changes by 8 over the first 7 items.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

options.text: The cost when 7 items have been produced is 8.
options.why: This describes $$C(7)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

options.text: The cost is increasing at a rate of 8 dollars per item when 7 items have been produced.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

questions.explanation: $$C'(7)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$C$$ when 7 items have been produced. Its sign (positive) says the cost is increasing, and its units are dollars per item.

questions.stem: The functions $$f$$, $$g$$, and $$h$$ satisfy $$g(x) \leq f(x) \leq h(x)$$ for all $$x$$, where $$g(x) = 4 - 4x^2$$ and $$h(x) = 4 + 4x^2$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$$?

options.why: Correct. Both $$g$$ and $$h$$ approach $$4$$ as $$x \to 0$$, so the Squeeze Theorem forces $$f$$ to approach $$4$$ too.
This adds the limits of $$g$$ and $$h$$; the squeeze gives their common value.

options.text: It cannot be determined without a formula for $$f$$.
options.why: The Squeeze Theorem determines the limit without a formula for $$f$$, because the bounds share the same limit.
This is the input value being approached, not the output.

questions.explanation: $$\lim_{x \to 0} g(x) = 4$$ and $$\lim_{x \to 0} h(x) = 4$$. Since $$f$$ is trapped between them, the Squeeze Theorem gives $$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = 4$$.

questions.stem: The base of a solid is the region bounded by $$y = \sqrt{x}$$, the x-axis, and $$x = 2$$. Cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are semicircles. What is the volume of the solid?

questions.stem: A farmer has 128 meters of fencing to enclose a rectangular field along a straight river. No fence is needed along the river. What is the largest possible area of the field, in square meters?

options.why: This makes all three fenced sides equal, which is not optimal.
This doesn't account for the two equal sides perpendicular to the river.
Correct. With width $$x$$ perpendicular to the river, $$A = x(128 - 2x)$$, maximized at $$x = 32$$.
This fences all four sides (a square), but the river side needs no fence.

questions.explanation: $$A(x) = x(128 - 2x)$$, $$A'(x) = 128 - 4x = 0$$ at $$x = 32$$, and $$A'' = -4 < 0$$, so this is a maximum. The dimensions are $$32$$ by $$64$$, with area $$2048$$.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = \frac{x^{2} + 4x - 5}{x^{2} + 7x + 10}$$. Which of the following lists every vertical asymptote of the graph of $$f$$?

options.why: $$x = -5$$ is a hole, because its factor cancels.

Correct. The factor $$x + 5$$ cancels, leaving a hole at $$x = -5$$. Only $$x = -2$$ makes the simplified denominator zero.
At $$x = -5$$ the numerator is also zero; the common factor cancels, giving a removable discontinuity (a hole), not an asymptote.

questions.explanation: Factor: $$f(x) = \frac{(x + 5)(x - 1)}{(x + 5)(x + 2)}$$. The common factor gives a hole at $$x = -5$$; near $$x = -2$$ the denominator approaches 0 while the numerator does not, so $$x = -2$$ is the only vertical asymptote.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2 - y$$ passing through the point $$(-2, 3)$$. What is $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at that point?

options.why: Correct. $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2x - \frac{dy}{dx}$$, and $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 1$$ at the point.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{2} - 2x$$. What value of $$c$$ satisfies the conclusion of the Mean Value Theorem for $$f$$ on the interval $$[-3, 3]$$?

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = 2x^{3} - 18x^{2} + 30x$$. At what value of $$x$$ does $$f$$ have a relative maximum?

questions.stem: Consider the curve $$x^2 - xy + y^2 = 48$$, for which $$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y - 2x}{2y - x}$$. At which points on the curve is the tangent line horizontal?

questions.stem: A 13-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 2 feet per second. How fast is the top of the ladder moving, in feet per second, when the bottom is 5 feet from the wall?

options.why: Correct. $$x^2 + y^2 = 169$$ gives $$x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$$. With $$x = 5$$, $$y = 12$$, $$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{5(2)}{12}$$.
The two ends do not move at the same speed; their rates depend on the position.
This swaps the roles of x and y.
The top slides down, so its rate is negative.

questions.explanation: Let $$x$$ be the distance from the wall and $$y$$ the height. $$2x x' + 2y y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x x'}{y} = -\frac{5 \cdot 2}{12} = -\frac{5}{6}$$ feet per second (the top is moving down).

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 21 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{3}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 7$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 107 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 7$$?

questions.stem: The function $$g$$ is defined by $$g(x) = \frac{\sin(5x)}{e^{4x} - 1}$$ for $$x \neq 0$$. For what value of $$g(0)$$ is $$g$$ continuous at $$x = 0$$?

options.why: Correct. Evaluating $$g$$ at inputs very close to 0 (or using the limits of $$\frac{\sin u}{u}$$ and $$\frac{e^u - 1}{u}$$) gives $$\frac{5}{4}$$.

Substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, which is indeterminate, not 0.

questions.stem: Let $$f(x) = x^{3} + 3x + e^{x/4}$$, and let $$g$$ be the inverse of $$f$$. What is the value of $$g'(11)$$?
